content: It includes citations for studies on HIV treatment, antiretroviral therapies, and related clinical trials. Each reference is described in a clear and structured manner: 1. Bucher HC, Guyatt GH, Griffith LE, Walter SD. This study analyzed the outcomes of direct and indirect treatment comparisons in meta-analyses of randomized controlled trials. Published in Medicine in 2010, the findings provide insights into methodological approaches for synthesizing evidence in clinical research. 2. Walmsley SL, Antela A, Clumeck N, et al. The efficacy of dolutegravir combined with abacavir-lamivudine for the treatment of HIV-1 infection was evaluated. Results published in the New England Journal of Medicine (Nov 7, 2013) demonstrated significant virological suppression and safety over 48 weeks. 3. Aberg JA, Tebas P, Overton ET, et al. A comparative study assessed the metabolic effects of darunavir/ritonavir versus atazanavir/ritonavir in treatment-naïve HIV-1-infected individuals over 48 weeks. Published in AIDS Research and Human Retroviruses (Oct 2012), the study highlighted differences in lipid profiles and other metabolic parameters. 4. Albini L, Cesana BM, Motta D, et al. A pilot randomized trial evaluated glomerular filtration rate (GFR) using creatinine or cystatin C in HIV-infected patients initiating tenofovir/emtricitabine with either atazanavir/ritonavir or efavirenz. Published in Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes (Jan 2012), the study provided insights into renal function monitoring in antiretroviral therapy. 5. Amin J, Becker S, Belloso W, et al.
